utterance: Hi Chloe, I'm the doctor today. I understand it burns when you wee. Can you tell me more about your symptoms and how they've changed since yesterday?
reply: It started yesterday morning, so about a day and a half ago. It really stings and burns, especially right at the end, and I am going constantly every half hour with only a little bit coming out and having to rush. It is a bit cloudy and smells, but I haven't seen any blood.

awards.label: How long the symptoms have been present
Colour of the urine or any visible blood

utterance: Have you had any fever, shivering, pain in your back or sides, nausea or vomiting? Any pain in your lower tummy, or trouble getting urine out at all?
reply: No fevers or shivers, and nothing in my back, just a bit of an ache low down in my tummy. I am eating normally and haven't been sick, and I don't have any trouble like that.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Fever, sweats, chills or shaking
Red flag excluded: Pain in the back or sides (loins)
Red flag excluded: Nausea, vomiting or feeling generally unwell
Red flag excluded: Abdominal pain beyond a low ache

utterance: Any vaginal discharge, itching, sores, or bleeding outside your usual period? Any pain during sex?
reply: I haven't had any discharge, itching, sores, or bleeding outside of my normal periods. Pain during sex has never been a problem either.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Any unusual vaginal bleeding

utterance: When was your last period, and was it normal? Could you be pregnant—for example, any missed pills, vomiting or diarrhoea affecting your pill?
reply: My last period was about two weeks ago and it was normal. I'm on the pill and I don't miss it, so I don't think I could be pregnant.

awards.label: Red flag excluded: Whether she could be pregnant

utterance: I ask everyone with these symptoms about sexual health, as some infections can feel similar. Have you had a new sexual partner recently, and do you use condoms?
reply: Um, yeah, I have a boyfriend; we've been together about a year and it is just him, and we don't use condoms because I am on the pill.

utterance: When did you last have a sexual health check, and have you or your boyfriend ever had a sexually transmitted infection? You mentioned a urine infection before—how often have these happened, and what treatment worked?
reply: I haven't had a check recently, and neither of us has ever had an infection like that. I only had one UTI about two years ago, and that's it.

utterance: Do you remember which antibiotic you had, and have you taken any antibiotics in the past three months? Any kidney problems or stones, diabetes, other health conditions, or medicines and supplements apart from your pill? Any medicine allergies?
reply: I don't remember which antibiotic I had back then, and I haven't taken any antibiotics this year. I don't have diabetes or any other health conditions, and I don't take any other medicines or supplements apart from my combined oral contraceptive pill. I'm not allergic to anything that I know of.

awards.label: Antibiotics in the last few months

utterance: This sounds most like a bladder infection. With your permission, I'll check your temperature and pulse, feel your tummy and check for tenderness over your kidneys. I'd also like a clean midstream urine sample: start weeing into the toilet, then catch some in the sample pot.
reply: Can't we just skip all that and give me a script? I really need to get back to work at the café.

utterance: I understand you're in a hurry. These checks only take a few minutes and help make sure it hasn't reached your kidneys or needs different treatment. We can keep this brief. Are you happy for me to do those checks and a quick urine test?
reply: Oh, okay then, if it's quick. Let's just get it done so I can get back.

finding: Soft. Mild suprapubic tenderness; non-tender elsewhere. No masses or organomegaly.
No renal angle tenderness on either side.

result: Leucocytes ++, nitrites positive, blood trace, protein trace. hCG not tested.

utterance: Your checks are reassuring, and the urine test supports a bladder infection. There are no signs of a kidney infection. I'd recommend a short course of antibiotics. Before choosing one, I'd like to check a urine pregnancy test, as pregnancy changes the treatment. Also, we offer chlamydia screening routinely to sexually active people under 30, even without symptoms. Would you be happy to have these tests?
reply: Oh, really? Do I have to do the pregnancy test too? I told you I never miss my pill.

utterance: No, you don't have to. Taking your pill reliably makes pregnancy very unlikely, so we can treat on that basis if you prefer. The sexual health screen is optional too and doesn't need to delay treatment. Would you like that screen, or leave it for now?
reply: I will just take the antibiotics now, please. Can I get that script so I can get back to my shift?

awards.label: First-line antibiotic: nitrofurantoin 100 mg 6-hourly for 5 days, fosfomycin 3 g once, or trimethoprim 300 mg daily for 3 days

utterance:
I've prescribed trimethoprim: one 300 mg tablet at night for three nights. Finish the course. It can occasionally cause nausea or a rash; get urgent help if you develop swelling or breathing trouble. It doesn't stop your pill working, but if you vomit or have severe diarrhoea, follow your pill's missed-pill advice and use condoms as directed.

Drink enough water to stay hydrated, don't hold your wee, and you can use paracetamol as directed on the packet for discomfort. You should start improving within 24–48 hours. If you're not clearly improving within 48 hours, or symptoms return after treatment, come back so we can send urine to the lab and review the antibiotic.

Get urgent medical care the same day for fever, shivering, back or side pain, vomiting, or worsening tummy pain. Go to emergency if you feel severely unwell or faint, or can't keep fluids down. If you miss your next period, take a pregnancy test and contact us if positive. A sexually transmitted infection hasn't been tested for today; please return for a screen if symptoms persist, or you develop discharge, pain during sex or unusual bleeding.
reply: Okay, thanks. I will grab the prescription on my way back to work.

awards.label: Acceptable, not ideal: Urethritis from a sexually transmitted infection in the can't-miss slot
